title: One Lesson, Many Readiness Levels
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Predict where one whole-class lesson should be pitched for a class spread across eight readiness levels, then move the pitch to see who is in reach.

educational.topic: The learning gap and whole-class instruction
learningObjectives: The learner will examine how the pitch of a single whole-class lesson determines how many students in a mixed-readiness class are in reach, too far behind, or already ahead, and identify the pitch that reaches the most students.
prerequisites: Learning gap, direct instruction, classroom, readiness as a grade level, and the "in reach" rule, from Chapter 1.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict, check, then explore one variable
keyQuestions: Which pitch puts the most students in reach?
How many students does the best pitch miss?
commonMisconceptions: Teaching to the middle reaches most of the class
A skilled enough teacher can find one pitch that works for everyone
Students ahead of the lesson are still learning something
assessmentOpportunities: Which pitch reaches the most students, and how many?
At pitch 7, how many find the lesson too hard?
Can one pitch reach the whole class?

controls.name: Q1 and Q2 boxes
controls.description: Type your predictions for the best pitch and the number of students it reaches.

controls.name: Check Q1 and Q2
controls.description: Checks both predictions. The pitch slider unlocks once both are checked.

controls.name: Pitch slider
controls.description: Sets the lesson pitch from grade 3 to grade 10 after it unlocks.

controls.name: Q3 box and Check Q3
controls.description: Type and check how many students find the pitch-7 lesson too hard.

controls.name: Reset
controls.description: Returns to the opening state with the pitch locked at 7.
